title: Terraform VPC lifecycle automation: health probes, safe upgrades, and routing-versioning
creator: Asha Iyer
description: Create a Terraform module and orchestration patterns for VPC network lifecycle automation focused on: synthetic health probes for subnets/endpoints, safe replacement paths for NAT/IGW changes, route-table versioning and canary rollouts, and drift detection for VPC endpoints. Module must be reusable across customer Private deployments and support non-disruptive upgrades and audit-friendly plan/apply workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for subnet topology (public/private/db), NAT/IGW consumption model, and VPC endpoint definitions (gateway+interface)
Automated synthetic health probes run per subnet and flag degraded paths (NAT failures, IGW blackholes, endpoint DNS failures)
Upgrade workflow supports plan-only validation, a canary apply to a single AZ, automated rollback on probe regression, and a final staged apply across remaining AZs
Route-table versioning: new route-table resource created for upgrades with traffic shifted via per-AZ association toggles and tagged history for audit
Safe NAT replacement pattern implemented (secondary NAT + connection draining + graceful failover) with zero expected connection loss for TCP/short-lived HTTP sessions
Terraform outputs include probe ARNs/URLs, route-version IDs, and a human-readable upgrade summary for runbooks
Module documented with example configs and an end-to-end e2e test harness that runs in CI (plan-only gating and a smoke test using ephemeral VPC)
technical_design: High-level design: a composable Terraform module that creates subnets, route tables, IGW/NAT topology, interface and gateway endpoints, and optional egress gateway functions. Attach small Lambda-backed synthetic probe suite (deployed as optional module subcomponent) that periodically validates egress paths and endpoint reachability. Introduce route-table resource naming/versioning pattern (rt-<logical>-v<semver-style>) and a canary-association resource to switch a single subnet to the new route table. Upgrade orchestration is handled by an orchestration script (Go) that performs: terraform plan -> dry-run validation using mocks -> apply to canary AZ -> wait for probe stability window -> gated apply to remaining AZs. Rollback uses route-version history and re-association. All changes are recorded to the deployment audit log (CloudTrail + internal console event).
implementation_plan: Week 1: Module scaffolding: inputs/outputs, subnet/rt/igw/nat/endpoint resources and docs
Week 2: Implement route-table versioning and canary association resource + write unit tests for resource naming and tagging
Week 3: Build optional synthetic probe stack (Lambda + CloudWatch Metrics + SNS alerts) and integrate probe outputs into TF outputs
Week 4: Orchestration tool (terraform-runner) enhancements: canary apply flow, plan-only gating, and automatic rollback hooks
Week 5: CI e2e harness: ephemeral VPC tests (plan-only for PRs, full apply in green CI) and runbook generation automation
Week 6: Internal dogfooding on a non-customer Private deployment, collect metrics and iterate on failover timings
infrastructure_changes: Create new optional module component: synthetic-probes (deploys Lambda functions and CloudWatch alarms)
Introduce new IAM roles for probes and orchestration tool with least-privilege apply pattern
Add tagging scheme: redwood:rt-version, redwood:upgrade-run-id for traceability
Optional S3 bucket for plan artifact storage and long-lived plan archives for audits
dependencies: ENG-61234 (networking-module-automated-upgrades-and-endpoint-health-ops) - re-use probe concepts and dashboards
security: KMS key for probe logs encryption
devops: CI runner capable of ephemeral VPC creation
testing_and_validation: Unit tests: terraform-compliance and kitchen-terraform checks for resource invariants
Integration: ephemeral VPC in CI that runs full apply for a small-scale topology and executes synthetic probes
Chaos test: intentionally remove NAT gateway to verify probe alarms and orchestration rollback
Performance test: measure median failover time for NAT swap across AZs and target < 60s for observed packet-level recovery
Security scan: terraform tfsec and custom policy checks for exposed endpoints and least-privilege IAM
rollout_and_upgrade_strategy: Preflight: terraform plan stored in S3 and reviewed by on-call/netops prior to apply
Canary: apply to a single AZ/subnet association using route-table canary-association resource
Stability window: 10 minutes of healthy probes (no new alarms) required to proceed
Batch apply: sequential AZ rollout with probe verification after each AZ
Rollback: on probe regression, run orchestration rollback that re-associates previous route-table IDs and reinstates previous NAT
Post-upgrade: tag final route-tables with stable: true and write a summary entry to the audit log
monitoring_and_alerting: CloudWatch metrics emitted by probes: egress_success_rate, endpoint_dns_ok, nat_health_score
Dashboards: per-customer VPC view with route-version timeline and probe success heatmap
Alerts: high-severity alert if any subnet's egress_success_rate < 99% for 5 minutes, auto-ticket creation to SRE channel
Synthetic probe SNS -> PagerDuty integration for on-call escalation
